_meta.note: What changed in the prototype, newest first, shown in the sidebar's What's new. Each item: kind (new, changed, removed), a short title, what it does and why, and where to see it. Add items with each change people will notice.

entries.summary: Documents work by phase, tasks put their tools and skills up front, and the first version narrows its scope.

items.title: Overview: the study at a glance, and similar studies
items.text: The Overview opens on a recap: the study type, the client and what the study covers, then where it stands. Four landmarks follow: the study type, the due date (in how many days, or late), the steps done out of the total with Continue on the phase in progress, and the budget. On the side, Similar studies lists the other studies of the same type, newest first, to see how the team ran them; another client’s study is for internal reference, its material stays in it.

items.title: Studies: a Lead column
items.text: The studies table names each study’s lead, its consultant, next to the client.

items.title: A status for each phase
items.text: Each phase of a study is To start, In progress, Done or Not needed. The analyst or the consultant changes it from the phase list or at the top of the phase; Steps says where the study stands (2 done, 1 in progress…), and Claude reads it with the phase.

items.title: Open the tools from the phase and the task
items.text: A task now reads top to bottom: what to do in a line, then where to do it (Open in Claude with its skill, Open Talkwalker, Open ICC…), then its deliverable. The top of a phase gathers its tools. The phase list counts each phase’s tools and skills (hover for their names).

items.title: Request a skill or automation: Claude checks first
items.text: From a step with no skill, say whether you need a skill (Claude does it with you) or an automation (it runs on its own). Claude first looks through the skills, the automations and the requests in progress: if something close exists, it shows it, with Open in Claude; if nothing does, the request goes straight to the tech team. In the prototype the check is scripted; the Claude skill that does it is still to build.

items.title: Tools read in the steps’ text
items.text: Steps that run frequencies, use the concordancer or work on the corpus facets now show the tool their text describes, marked “to confirm”: the method files describe the work without naming the tool. Facets are created in the Corpus Manager and read in the ICC. The method owner confirms each link in one click, or removes it. The Files tool joins the tool repository.

items.title: Edit where you read
items.text: No more forms opening inside a panel. What you can change shows a pencil on hover: click the text, type, Enter saves, Escape cancels. To add, a dashed “+” row turns into a field in place. To remove, a small cross, with Undo for a few seconds. Choosing (a phase document, a teammate) opens a short list next to the button. Each panel says at the top what your role can change and what stays locked.

items.title: ICC in Tools
items.text: The ICC joins the tool repository, linked to the steps that use it: collecting reviews (R&R), building a corpus, running frequencies.

items.title: Request a skill
items.text: A step with no skill offers “Request a skill”: say what Claude should do there and which tools it needs a connector for. The request lands with the tech team, who build the connectors and the skill; once Fabien validates it, the skill is available to everyone and linked to its step.

items.title: One document per phase
items.text: Each phase works in one document of the study: a working sheet, a deck, a queries tab. Open a phase and choose it among the study’s documents, or add it there and then (a link, an upload, or a copy of the template the phase uses). Claude reads it with the phase.

items.title: Files is the study’s document space
items.text: Files lists every document of the study and the phases that work in it. Add a document here and pick it in any phase; one document can serve several phases.

items.title: Tools and skills on each task, at a glance
items.text: A task shows its skill with an Open in Claude button and its tools as buttons that open the tool. Its output reads under it. “How to do it, the check” opens the rest of the method’s columns.

items.title: Skills
items.text: The skills we have in Claude, what each does, its status, and the steps of each study type that use it. Files to the Corpus Manager now sits on the steps that load or build a corpus.

items.title: What’s new
items.text: This page. A New badge in the sidebar shows until you have read the latest changes.

items.title: Set aside for the first version
items.text: Ticking tasks, validating phases, time tracking, Oversight and the automatic Slack channel. Studies still carry their notes, added tasks, documents and team.

entries.summary: The 18 methods are in, and studies, study types and tools each have their page.

items.title: Studies
items.text: One table of every study, not only yours: study, client, study type, family, status, due date. Filter by family, study type, status or person to see how a study of the same type was run.

items.title: Study types (formerly Methods)
items.text: The 18 methods of the M&T and SML method files, with their phases and tasks as written. Each study type says what it is and the question it answers; drafts are marked as such.

items.title: Tools
items.text: The tools we work in, by kind, each with the steps of each study type that use it. A study type’s owner links or unlinks a tool from a step.

items.title: Tasks fold to one line
items.text: A phase lists its tasks in short; open one to read how to do it, the check and the points to watch.

items.title: Access code
items.text: The prototype asks for an access code before any page. Ask the Semantiweb team for it.
